title: This Crab's Blue Blood Is Worth $60,000 a Gallon

scenes.text: A crab with blood worth sixty thousand dollars a gallon.
It's bright blue, because copper carries its oxygen, not iron.
Near a bacterial toxin it clots instantly. Labs use that to test vaccines and IV drugs.
Every batch of COVID vaccine was tested for toxins, by law. This blood is how.
Each year hundreds of thousands are caught, bled of a third of their blood, then released.
It's been here 450 million years, long before dinosaurs. Blue blood, sixty thousand dollars a gallon.

description:
Horseshoe crab blood is bright blue, clots almost instantly around bacterial toxins, and has been valued at around 60,000 dollars a gallon.
The pharmaceutical industry has used it since the 1960s to check vaccines, injectable drugs and implants for contamination. Hundreds of thousands of crabs are bled each year, losing up to a third of their blood before being returned to the sea, and the species has existed for about 450 million years. A synthetic alternative was approved in the United States in 2024.
Should we keep using the crabs, or switch to the synthetic test? Comment below.
first_comment: Horseshoe crabs aren't actually crabs. They're closer to spiders and scorpions. Would you rather keep bleeding them, or trust the synthetic test that replaces their blood?
